key_insight: A curriculum masking strategy for single‑encoder masked modeling substantially strengthens cross‑attention between melody and harmony, yielding harmonizations that follow melodic cues more closely and generalize better to out‑of‑domain melodies.
problem_solved: Existing diffusion‑inspired training curricula for single‑encoder harmonization produce weak cross‑attention and under‑exploit melodic information, leading to poor melodic fidelity and limited generalization.
method: Design a curriculum masking schedule that progressively controls which melody and harmony tokens are masked during training to encourage melody→harmony information flow.
Train a single‑encoder transformer with a masked reconstruction objective while using attention‑aware masking to boost cross‑attention between melodic and harmonic segments.
Evaluate via attention analysis, objective metrics and listening tests to show improved melodic adherence and out‑of‑domain robustness.
impact: A simple training curriculum unlocks better use of melodic cues in single‑encoder harmonization models, improving harmonization quality and robustness; the approach is lightweight and can be applied to other sequence tasks needing stronger cross‑modal or cross‑segment attention.
visual_elements: Curriculum timeline: a sequence showing mask density/type changing over epochs (early heavy masking → later selective exposure of melody).
Attention heatmaps before vs. after curriculum (melody tokens on one axis, harmony on the other) to visualize strengthened cross‑attention.
Single‑encoder transformer schematic with masked tokens highlighted and arrows showing melody→harmony attention flow.
Side‑by‑side piano-roll examples and short audio spectrograms of input melody + baseline vs. curriculum harmonizations.
paper_title: Pay (Cross) Attention to the Melody: Curriculum Masking for Single-Encoder Melodic Harmonization
paper_authors: Maximos Kaliakatsos-Papakostas, Dimos Makris, Konstantinos Soiledis, Konstantinos-Theodoros Tsamis, Vassilis Katsouros
